claims.board_facts: Displayed coordinates, capture rays, actors and passes agree with legal replay.
claims.analysis: A choice explanation is supported by the stated search settings or by complete rule checks within an explicit horizon.
claims.learning: A beginner can make and explain the relevant choice in an unseen position. Correctly recalling a recommendation is insufficient.

player_account.handling: Save the first statement with the recorded move, collection time and whether this position already had application analysis. Keep it separate from verified facts. Do not infer original intent or a misconception from a move alone.
player_account.exposure_limit: Application availability does not establish what the learner actually saw; external analysis and prior knowledge are unknown.

procedure: Freeze the complete case list and criteria before reviewing results. Include forced, tied, highest-rated, lower-rated, pass and corner positions from independent complete games.
Give a qualified Othello reviewer only the independent board and history packet first. Record preferred moves, concrete reasons and search settings before opening the application evidence packet.
Check all displayed facts and every claim in the second packet, including what the player actually asked. Record counterexamples and corrections; missing review fields are unreviewed.
Reproduce relevant branches with a separately implemented engine where available. Solve tractable endings completely. Midgame engine agreement is corroboration, not proof.
An earlier revision is relevant only when a verified alternative changes the opportunity under discussion. Nearest prior choice and later outcome alone do not establish causation.
independent_review.failure_policy: Any false board fact or overstated forced claim fails that case. Report each criterion separately; an unexplained score gap cannot pass as a causal explanation.

learning_evaluation.design: Assign target beginners to conditions before exposure. Record baseline choices and reasons, then assess matched unseen positions with identical prompts and no recommendations or immediate feedback. Reviewers grade reasons without seeing condition assignment.
learning_evaluation.separation: Use different complete source games for teaching, practice, baseline and post-assessment. Exclude color swaps, rotations and reflections across sets. Freeze the assessment before data collection and keep answers unavailable to participants.
learning_evaluation.capture_mechanism: Use capture-lines-v1 for move and friendly-anchor accuracy. This measures a local mechanism only.

decision_reason_rubric.0: The reason contradicts board facts or has no relevant mechanism.
decision_reason_rubric.1: Identifies a relevant opportunity but does not compare what changes between choices.
decision_reason_rubric.2: Explains a verified difference between choices using squares, captures and an opponent reply, within the evidence's scope.

learning_evaluation.completion: An export, automated test, model agreement or successful replay cannot establish learning. No expert review or controlled learner study is reported as completed.

earlier_connection.eligibility: The recorded own-turn decision has a corner threat that the opponent can force within its next two turns under every current defense.
earlier_connection.search: Trace every actual state backwards while the same bounded corner threat remains. At the earlier human choice that permits a defense, compare the recorded move only with the canonical highest-rated recommendation. Require a strict score advantage and a rule-verified defense under that recommendation; do not invent a preference among tied recorded best moves.
earlier_connection.evidence: Retain native candidate scores and settings, the forcing certificate for the recorded move, refutations for all opponent first replies under the recommendation, and every intervening revision and actor. The bound is three plies from an opponent turn and at most four from a defender turn, with legal passes included.
earlier_connection.interface: Offer navigation only for a verified connection. A negative result establishes no related pair within this scope; it does not establish that the corner or final loss was unavoidable throughout the game.
earlier_connection.limits: A bounded defense does not establish permanent corner safety, explain the full search-score difference, or predict a different result. An unrelated earlier turn, shared target alone, and nearest previous choice are insufficient.
earlier_connection.navigation: Prepare the linked native lesson without calling a language model. Report its coaching status as not_requested until the learner explicitly requests coaching or asks a question. Reuse a prior saved analysis when it already exists.
earlier_connection.snapshot_binding: When a previously unplayed turn becomes recorded history, bind the same native scores to the actual move and reset outdated coaching. Preserve the original player account and its source.

comparison_focus.requirement: The recommended line must demonstrate a defense against the same corner discussed in the comparison, even when the recommendation also has a different corner threat.
comparison_focus.other_risks: Retain certificates for other forced corners in the recommendation, state those risks separately, and never present a defensive refutation as a positive attack certificate.
comparison_focus.passes_and_terminal_lines: Represent mandatory passes and game termination explicitly; neither is a freely chosen defensive move.

assessment_preparation.sources: Four fresh complete native Edax level-1 games, each with eight seeded random opening plies. Keep the generated seed and source games in the private answer packet. These are generated sources, not independent expert annotations.
assessment_preparation.forms: Two forms with eight questions each: two anchor, two recapture, two capture-line and two reply-access questions. Each form uses different complete games. Equal objective counts do not establish equal difficulty; descriptors are retained for review.
assessment_preparation.exclusion: Reject any selected board matching a known teaching/practice board or any state of the other form, including rotations, reflections and color swaps. Include the actual study teaching games with --exclude-games; the default checks known project samples and the shipped practice bank only.
assessment_preparation.administration: Give each participant the assigned form before teaching and the other after teaching, with identical instructions, no recommendations and no immediate feedback. Keep the private answer and allocation packets away from participants. Preparation defaults to zero enrolled participants.
assessment_preparation.allocation: With --participants, freeze randomized blocks of four balancing both teaching condition and form order. Preserve the assigned schedule prefix if enrolling additional participants.
assessment_preparation.grading: Use the grade command for one participant at a time. Retain every assigned question in the denominator and all missing answers. Grade only the first recorded attempt. Export shuffled reason packets without form, condition, source-game or automatic-score fields; the evaluator retains their separate mapping.
assessment_preparation.status: Preparation is automatic. Expert review, empirical form equivalence and learner benefit remain unverified. Development contract tests do not count as participant results.
